QF.id: AIF Valuation Taxation and Good Practices_67

answer.text: Estimating terminal/exit value and discounting back to present value at the estimated hurdle or discount rate
Using bond yields as discount rate

explanation.text: The Logic: The VC method estimates a terminal/exit value at an expected exit horizon and discounts it back to present value at the estimated hurdle or discount rate. The XIX-A workbook illustration uses a 40% expected return as the discount rate. The Trap: Current book value ignores the discounted-cashflow logic of the VC method, bond yields are not the hurdle rate used for venture investments, and IP-only valuation is not what the method describes. Note: The "30-70% target return" range is not supported by the workbook; the supported approach is terminal value discounted at the estimated hurdle/discount rate.
